# Native Windows installer-context diagnostic

The actual c41 run 37758310432 completed build and discovery normally. Discovery took 82.328 seconds and preserved all 674 native names, including the 666-name baseline. All ten intended tests completed: seven passed and three invocation tests failed. Five pool tests and the receipt-rotation test passed. Independent receipt-policy verification is a separate gate.

Each invocation failure occurred during fixture provisioning, at installation validation. The installed `vswhere` query completed with exit 0 and zero stdout bytes. No native client compilation or provider dispatch occurred. That identifies an empty selection; it does not identify why the selection was empty.

The old unanchored diagnostic filter also selected the three existing `RCIRInvocationBindingTests`, all of which passed. Its strict ten-case collector correctly rejected the unexpected count. The filter now anchors the exact target and class names. A negative control compares the filter with the frozen native baseline and rejects similar class names. This diagnostic correction removes no source tests and does not replace the required full current-candidate suite.

The new read-only A/B/A probe uses the same installed query executable and seven fixed arguments under three profiles: the three-key minimal environment, that environment plus an explicit bounded installer context, and the minimal environment again. The only additional names permitted are `ALLUSERSPROFILE`, `ProgramData`, `ProgramFiles`, and `ProgramFiles(x86)`. Missing values remain absent. Values must be bounded local absolute Windows paths. PATH, credentials, user-profile variables and the rest of the ambient environment are excluded.

The probe uses Python native subprocess transport, not the production Foundation invocation. Each query has a five-second deadline and a 32 KiB stdout retention ceiling. An unchanged owned Windows Job Object supervisor contains the entire probe under a 45-second ceiling. Standard error is discarded. Only fixed profile labels, presence flags, validation flags, counts, hashes, outcomes and timings are uploaded in a separate closed artifact. No environment values, filesystem paths or query output are printed or uploaded. The installed query binary is hashed before and after the three samples.

A difference would establish a read-only diagnostic environment counterfactual on that native runner. It would not establish a production repair, justify broad environment inheritance, or prove Kafka/Kubernetes operation. Production environment and the reviewed source f07 / Sources fd3f remain unchanged. Any reusable host-context primitive must be justified by the actual native result and separately validated through the production boundary.
